notes: Profile: Mid-market B2B SaaS building a product-recommendation & support overlay. Heavy chat+embedding mix: interactive UI for end-customers + nightly reranking pipelines.
Primary ask: validate unit economics at scale before committing to Dedicated. Wants hosted API as low-friction POC path, then move to Dedicated if economics justify.
Performance targets: 95th pctile <= 250ms for chat responses under normal traffic; batch rerank jobs throughput ~2k qps during nightly windows.
Cost sensitivity: high. Finance VP quote: "need predictable sub-$250k total annual spend for inference or we can't sign a 1yr commit" — targeting $100k-300k ARR with predictability.
Model preferences: open models (Llama 2 / Falcon family) with 4-bit quant_PROFILE for cost tests; willing to test Redwood-verified quantized variants.
Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variant during load spikes; must preserve top-k reranking quality within 1.5% baseline drop.
Security: require SOC2-level controls, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and per-route audit logging. Data residency: prefer regional US residency for EU customers (question raised).

Workshop outcomes (2/14): SE recommended aggressive prefix caching for chat history (50-70% cache hit expected), batching config for reranker (batch sizes 64-256 depending on model), and try q4_0 quant profile for nightly jobs.
POC metrics: measure tokens/sec, avg latency (p50/p95), cache hit rate, effective cost per 1k tokens, and rerank NDCG delta vs baseline.
Quote from CTO on post-workshop call: "If Redwood Optimize can move unit cost by 3-4x without quality loss, Dedicated's ROI is clear."
Commercial ask: example committed capacity pricing and a migration path (hosted -> dedicated) that keeps routing/observability intact.
